facts.statement: Charonosaurus was a very large hadrosaur estimated to be around 10 meters in length and 5 metric tons in body mass.
facts.quote: Charonosaurus is a very large lambeosaurine hadrosaur, estimated around 10 m in length and 5 MT in body mass.

facts.statement: Charonosaurus likely possessed a long, backward-projecting hollow crest similar to Parasaurolophus, supported by highly modified frontal bones.
facts.quote: The partial skull resembles that of Parasaurolophus and probably had a similar long, backward-projecting hollow crest, indicated by the highly modified dorsal surface of the frontal bones.

facts.statement: The femur of Charonosaurus could reach 1.35 meters in length, longer than any other known hadrosaur of its time except Shantungosaurus giganteus.
facts.quote: El fémur podría tener 1,35 metros de longitud, más que todos los otros hadrosáuridos conocidos en su tiempo, con la excepción de Shantungosaurus giganteus.

facts.statement: Adult Charonosaurus had approximately 40 rows of teeth in the lower jaw, with only one to two teeth in use at a time.
facts.quote: En la mandíbula inferior había especímenes adultos de aproximadamente 40 filas de dientes de dos a tres dientes, de los cuales uno a dos dientes estaban en uso simultáneamente.

facts.statement: The lower jaw teeth of Charonosaurus were very high, with dental crowns reaching up to 40 millimeters in height.
facts.quote: Los dientes de la mandíbula inferior eran muy altos con coronas dentales de hasta 40 milímetros de alto.

facts.statement: The sacrum of Charonosaurus consisted of nine fused vertebrae.
facts.quote: El sacro consta de nueve vértebras fusionadas.

facts.statement: Charonosaurus fossils were described by Godefroit, Zan, and Jin in 2000 from the south bank of the Amur River.
facts.quote: Its fossils were described by Godefroit, Zan, and Jin in 2000, on the south bank of the Amur River, dividing China from Russia.

facts.statement: In 2000, Pascal Godefroit, Shuqin Zan, and Liyong Jin erected the species Charonosaurus jiayinensis, designating CUST J-V1251-57 as the holotype.
facts.quote: In 2000, Pascal Godefroit, Shuqin Zan and Liyong Jin erected a new genus and species, Charonosaurus jiayinensis, to accommodate the Yuliangze material, and designated CUST J-V1251-57 as the holotype specimen.

facts.statement: Charonosaurus is a monotypic genus consisting only of the species C. jiayinensis.
facts.quote: It is monotypic, consisting of the species, C. jiayinensis.

facts.statement: Charonosaurus is known from the Late Maastrichtian Yuliangze Formation in Heilongjiang Province, northeastern China.
facts.quote: It is known from a partial skull (Holotype: CUST J-V1251-57 (Changchun University of Sciences and Technology, Changchun, Jilin Province, China) found in the Late Maastrichtian Yuliangze Formation, west of Jiayin village, Heilongjiang Province, northeastern China.

facts.statement: Charonosaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous, between approximately 69.9 and 66 million years ago, in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, entre aproximadamente 69,9 a 66 millones de años, durante el Maastrichtiense, en lo que es hoy Asia.

facts.statement: Abundant ejected teeth from carnivorous dinosaurs suggest Charonosaurus carcasses were consumed by predators and scavengers or that the animals were killed during river hunts.
facts.quote: The abundance of ejected teeth from carnivorous dinosaurs shows that carcasses of Charonosaurus were torn up and consumed by predators and scavengers and/or that Charonosaurus was killed by these predators on hunts along a river.

facts.statement: A 2021 study by Ramírez-Velasco et al. placed Charonosaurus closer to Tlatolophus and Blasisaurus than to Parasaurolophus.
facts.quote: A study by Ramírez-Velasco et al. in 2021 place Charonosaurus closer to Tlatolophus and Blasisaurus than to Parasaurolophus.

facts.statement: There is an ongoing debate regarding the exact phylogenetic placement of Charonosaurus, with different studies yielding conflicting results.
facts.quote: The following phylogeny was conducted by Penélope Cruzado-Caballero et al. in 2013.

facts.statement: The genus name Charonosaurus is derived from Charon, the Greek mythological ferryman of the dead, and the Greek word for lizard.
facts.quote: The genus name is derived from Charon, the ferryman from Greek mythology who carried the dead across the dead river Acheron (or Styx), and the ancient Greek "sauros" (lizard).

facts.statement: Fossils of Charonosaurus were discovered in 1975 near the city of Jiayin in the Amur region.
facts.quote: Los restos de Charonosaurus provienen de grandes lechos huesos que se han descubierto en 1975 durante las excavaciones de varias instituciones chinas en las cercanías de la ciudad de Jiayin en Amur

facts.statement: The species was formally described in 2000 based on a partial skeleton found in the Yuliangze Formation in Heilongjiang, China.
facts.quote: llevándose a cabo la descripción en el 2000, a partir de un esqueleto parcial encontrado en el oeste de la villa Jiayin, provincia de Heilongjiang al noreste de China, en la Formación Yuliangze

facts.statement: The orientation of long bones suggests they were transported and deposited by a river.
facts.quote: Los huesos largos tienden hacia una cierta orientación, de la cual se concluye que los huesos fueron transportados y depositados por un río

facts.statement: Dinosaur teeth found in bone beds indicate that some individuals were killed by predators or eaten by scavengers.
facts.quote: Los dientes de los terópodos en los lechos de huesos indican que fueron muertos por los depredadores o que los cadáveres fueron devorados por los carroñeros

facts.statement: The holotype is a partial skull housed at the University of Science and Technology of Changchun, described by Pascal Godefroit, Shuqin Zan, and Liyong Jin.
facts.quote: El holotipo, un cráneo parcial, es CUST J-V1251-57, se encuentra en la universidad de Ciencias y Tecnologías de Changchun, Changchun, provincia de Jilin y fue descrito por Pascal Godefroit, Shuqin Zan y Liyong Jin como C. jiayinensis

facts.statement: Remains of adults and juveniles found in the same area provide information on the postcranial skeleton, including a femur length of 1.35 meters.
facts.quote: Los restos de adultos y jóvenes se han descubiertos en la misma área y formación representando probablemente la misma especie y es fuente de información sobre la mayor parte del esqueleto postcraneal, la longitud del fémur era de 1,35 metros

facts.statement: The partial skull resembles that of Parasaurolophus, featuring a hollow crest projecting backward over a highly modified frontal bone.
facts.quote: El cráneo parcial se asemeja al de Parasaurolophus y tenía probablemente un largo similar, con una cresta hueca proyectada hacia atrás, que pasa por la superficie dorsal altamente modificada del hueso frontal

facts.statement: Charonosaurus is one of the largest known hadrosaurs in Asia.
facts.quote: Charonosaurus es uno de los hadrosáuridos más grandes conocidos actualmente en Asia

facts.statement: Charonosaurus indicates that lambeosaurines survived until the end of the Cretaceous, a time when this group is not known from North America.
facts.quote: Charonosaurus es uno de los hadrosáuridos más grandes conocidos actualmente en Asia e indica que los lambeosaurinos sobrevivieron hasta el final del Cretácico; este grupo no se conoce del Maastrichtiense en Norteamérica

facts.statement: Hadrosaur bones from the formation were previously described by Anatoly Riabinin as Mandschurosaurus amurensis.
facts.quote: Entre ellos se encuentran los huesos de hadrosáuridos, que fueron descritos por Anatoly Riabinin como Mandschurosaurus amurensis

facts.statement: Anatoly Riabinin also described a fragmentary hadrosaur ischium as Saurolophus krystofovici.
facts.quote: Riabinin además describió otro ejemplar un muy fragmentario isquion de hadrosáurido y lo llamó Saurolophus krystofovici

facts.statement: Both names previously assigned to fossils from this formation are now considered nomina dubia.
facts.quote: Ambos nombres ahora se enumeran como nomina dubia

facts.statement: The genus name Charonosaurus is derived from Charon, the Greek mythological ferryman of the dead, and sauros, meaning lizard.
facts.quote: El nombre del género Charonosaurus deriva de Caronte, Charon, el barquero de la mitología griega, que transportaba los muertos en el río de los muertos estigia , y los sauros, lagarto

facts.statement: The specific epithet jiayinensis refers to the type locality, the site of Jiayin.
facts.quote: El epíteto específico jiayinensis se refiere a la localidad tipo, el sitio de Jiayin

facts.statement: A 2000 cladistic analysis based on skull, teeth, and postcranial features shows Charonosaurus jiayinensis is most closely related to Parasaurolophus among Lambeosaurinae.
facts.quote: Un análisis cladístico realizado en 2000 por Pascal Godefroit, Shuqin Zan Liyong Jin, y sobre la base del cráneo, dientes, y las características postcraneales muestra que Charonosaurus jiayinensis filogenéticamente está más estrechamente relacionado con Parasaurolophus que cualquiera de los otros Lambeosaurinae

facts.statement: Within the subfamily Lambeosaurinae, Charonosaurus and Parasaurolophus are closely related in the tribe Parasaurolophini.
facts.quote: Dentro de la subfamilia Lambeosaurinae Charonosaurus y Parasaurolophus están estrechamente relacionados en la tribu Parasaurolophini

facts.statement: The parent group of Charonosaurus is Parasaurolophini.
facts.quote: Parent group: Parasaurolophini

facts.statement: Charonosaurus belongs to the family Hadrosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Hadrosauridae

facts.statement: Charonosaurus is classified in the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: Charonosaurus lived during the Maastrichtian stage, between 72.2 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)
